parameters.name: userID
parameters.description: ID of the signed-in user. `me` is also accepted; another user's ID is refused with 403

name.description: Name to tell the token apart, 1 to 100 characters, unique among your tokens ignoring case

expires_on.description: Expiry as an ISO date and time in the future; null for no expiry; left out for 90 days

visibility.description: Which items the token sees: `user` only the items you created (default), `all` every item (only when your own visibility is all)

proxy_hosts.description: Level for Proxy Hosts: manage, view or hidden

redirection_hosts.description: Level for Redirection Hosts: manage, view or hidden

dead_hosts.description: Level for 404 Hosts: manage, view or hidden

streams.description: Level for Streams: manage, view or hidden

access_lists.description: Level for Access Lists: manage, view or hidden

certificates.description: Level for Certificates: manage, view or hidden

permissions.description: Level for each section: manage, view or hidden. A level above your own is refused with 400

admin.description: Whether the token acts as an administrator for the admin areas; only an administrator can turn it on. Default false

allow_delete.description: Whether the token may delete (DELETE requests, replace restores, MCP delete tools). Default false

201.description: The created token, with the token text in `token`, shown once

400.description: Refused: the name is empty, longer than 100 characters or already used, the expiry is not a future date, the body is invalid, or a level or visibility is above the owner's

403.description: Not allowed: the request was made with an API token, the user in the path is not the signed-in user, or an Administrator token was asked for by a non-administrator

description:
Creates a token for the signed-in user. The answer holds the token text once in `token`; it is never shown again, so copy it now. A token never has more than its owner: a level or visibility above the owner's is refused with 400, `admin` only for administrators. `expires_on` left out gives 90 days (the web interface offers 30, 90 or 365 days, a date or none); a name that you already use is refused with 400.

Needs: a signed-in session (API tokens are refused)
